Basic Economic Concepts: The value of the next best alternative forgone
A model of the maximum output combinations available
Resources are not equally suited to all uses, bowing the curve outward
Producing at a lower opportunity cost than another party
Producing more output from the same resources
Concentrating on what you produce at lowest opportunity cost
The additional satisfaction from one more unit
The additional cost of producing one more unit
Continue an activity while marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost
The set of rules a society uses to allocate scarce resources
Supply and Demand: Law of demand
Quantity demanded falls as price rises, all else equal
Law of supply
Quantity supplied rises as price rises, all else equal
Change in quantity demanded
Movement along the demand curve caused by a price change
Change in demand
A shift of the whole curve caused by a non-price factor
Determinants of demand
Income, tastes, related good prices, expectations, and buyer numbers
Substitute good
A good whose price rise increases demand for another
Complement good
A good whose price rise decreases demand for another
Normal good
A good whose demand rises with income
Inferior good
A good whose demand falls as income rises
Market equilibrium
The price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
Surplus
Excess supply occurring when price sits above equilibrium
Shortage
Excess demand occurring when price sits below equilibrium
Price elasticity of demand
The percentage change in quantity over the percentage change in price
Consumer surplus
The difference between willingness to pay and the price actually paid
Producer surplus
The difference between the price received and the minimum acceptable price
Price ceiling
A legal maximum price that creates shortages when binding
Price floor
A legal minimum price that creates surpluses when binding
Deadweight loss
The lost total surplus when output deviates from the efficient level
Production, Cost, and the Perfect Compet: Total product
The total output produced with a given quantity of inputs
Marginal product
The extra output from one more unit of a variable input
Law of diminishing marginal returns
Marginal product eventually falling as an input is added
Fixed cost
A cost that does not vary with output in the short run
Variable cost
A cost that changes as output changes
Average total cost
Total cost divided by quantity produced
Marginal cost curve shape
It crosses average total cost at its minimum point
Economies of scale
Long-run average cost falling as output expands
Diseconomies of scale
Long-run average cost rising as a firm grows too large
Accounting versus economic profit
Revenue minus explicit costs versus minus explicit and implicit costs
Perfect competition
Many firms, identical products, and free entry and exit
Price taker
A firm facing a perfectly elastic demand curve at market price
Profit maximizing rule
Produce where marginal revenue equals marginal cost
Shutdown rule
Shut down in the short run if price falls below average variable cost
Long-run equilibrium in perfect competition
Zero economic profit with price equal to minimum average total cost
Allocative efficiency
Producing where price equals marginal cost
Productive efficiency
Producing at the minimum of average total cost
Imperfect Competition: Monopoly
A single seller of a product with no close substitutes
Barrier to entry
Any obstacle preventing new firms from entering a market
Natural monopoly
A market where one firm can supply at lower cost than several
Marginal revenue under monopoly
It lies below the demand curve because price must fall to sell more
Monopoly inefficiency
Producing where price exceeds marginal cost, creating deadweight loss
Price discrimination
Charging different buyers different prices for the same good
Perfect price discrimination
Capturing all consumer surplus by charging each buyer their maximum
Monopolistic competition
Many firms selling differentiated products with free entry
Excess capacity
Monopolistically competitive firms producing below minimum average cost
Oligopoly
A market dominated by a few interdependent firms
Game theory
The analysis of strategic decisions among interdependent players
Payoff matrix
A table showing outcomes for each combination of strategies
Dominant strategy
A choice best regardless of what the rival does
Nash equilibrium
An outcome where no player benefits from changing alone
Collusion and cartel
Firms cooperating to restrict output and raise price
Antitrust policy
Government action to prevent or break up excessive market power
Factor Markets: Factor market
The market where firms buy labour, land, and capital
Derived demand
Demand for an input arising from demand for the output
Marginal revenue product
The extra revenue from hiring one more unit of an input
Marginal factor cost
The extra cost of hiring one more unit of an input
Hiring rule
Hire until marginal revenue product equals marginal factor cost
Perfectly competitive labour market
Many firms and workers, with the wage set by the market
Monopsony
A market with a single buyer of an input
Monopsony outcome
Employing fewer workers at a lower wage than a competitive market
Least-cost rule
Allocating spending so marginal product per dollar is equal across inputs
Substitution effect in factor markets
Replacing an input whose price has risen with a cheaper one
Determinants of labour supply
Wages elsewhere, preferences, and the number of qualified workers
Minimum wage in a competitive market
A binding floor creating a surplus of labour
Market Failure and the Role of Governmen: A situation where free markets fail to allocate resources efficiently
A cost or benefit falling on someone outside the transaction
A spillover cost causing overproduction relative to the social optimum
Private cost plus any external cost
Private benefit plus any external benefit
A tax set equal to the external cost to internalise it
A payment raising output toward the socially optimal level
A good that is nonrival and nonexcludable
People consuming a public good without paying for it
A rival but nonexcludable good prone to overuse
Depletion of a shared resource from individually rational overuse
A tax taking a larger share of income as income rises
A tax taking a smaller share of income as income rises
A graph of cumulative income share against cumulative population share
A single number from zero to one measuring income inequality
